claims.text: Apple’s security releases index says the latest version of macOS is 26.6.2 and lists macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 with a release date of August 17, 2026.

evidence_passages.text: As of August 27, 2026, Apple’s security-releases index says “The latest version of macOS is 26.6.2” and lists macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 with a release date of August 17, 2026.

claims.text: Apple’s security-content page says macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 is available for macOS Tahoe.

evidence_passages.text: Apple’s security-content page for macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 says the update was released August 17, 2026 and is “Available for: macOS Tahoe.”

claims.text: In the supplied Apple-page evidence for macOS Tahoe 26.6.2, Apple does not identify any actively exploited issues.
acceptable_patterns: does not state that any issue .* may have been exploited
Apple does not identify any actively exploited issues

evidence_passages.text: Regarding Active Exploitation: No, Apple does not state that any issue "may have been exploited" in this document.
I found no Apple statement on either page identifying any actively exploited issue in macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 or Safari 26.6.1.

rejected_claims.text: Safari 26.6.1 is Apple’s most recent macOS security update.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence treats this as an ambiguity: Safari 26.6.1 is a newer Mac-related security release, but the best-supported macOS OS update is macOS Tahoe 26.6.2.

rejected_claims.text: Apple identified CVE-2026-65400 as actively exploited.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence says outside parties reported exploitation, but Apple’s own pages do not state that the issue may have been exploited.

rejected_claims.text: macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 affects macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence says macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 is "Available for: macOS Tahoe," while Sonoma and Sequoia are listed for Safari 26.6.1.
